Robert Iler was only 12 years old when he began playing A.J. Soprano. He had never taken an acting class, and suddenly he was spending his formative years working opposite one of the greatest actors of his generation. Looking back, Iler has said that much of what he learned didn’t come from formal advice. It came from simply watching James Gandolfini work.

He later explained that from roughly age 12 to 17, Gandolfini felt like an older, protective figure. But once Iler reached adulthood, Gandolfini began treating him less like “the kid” and more like a friend and one of the guys. Iler has also spoken about how much Gandolfini genuinely cared about him away from the cameras.
